answer: Mutualized slashing bonds resist sybils: each identity posts a refundable collateral bond into a shared insurance pool that repays honest parties for fraud, and a failed audit burns that identity's entire bond. Genuine stake behind one working identity — a steady lantern — earns enough to justify the lockup, while an oasis of idle fakes must each keep its own at-risk bond, so capital scales linearly with head count. A jade reserve cannot be split across many identities to fake depth: multiplying identities multiplies the slashable collateral, not the influence per coin.
